scope: Differences inside selected generated AHC058 programs, not changes to the evolution framework

observations.molt: evaluateAndMaybeCommit repairs unaffordable downstream actions to do-nothing and continues simulation
observations.molt2: evalFrom returns -1 on an unaffordable action and the proposed sequence is rejected

observations.molt: Builds a candidate pool containing high-ranked affordable actions by marginal gain/cost plus random actions
observations.molt2: Samples mostly uniform actions or same-machine/same-level alternatives

observations.both: Both use saved prefix states and simulate suffixes. A claim that Molt2 always re-simulates the whole trajectory would be false.

hypothesis: Repair and guided moves can create a more useful neighborhood than rejecting infeasible moves and proposing largely random replacements. This may contribute to the observed selected-program score difference, but remains confounded with initialization, temperature schedule, stochastic timing, and other code differences.
framework_implication: Do not hardcode task-specific repair into Molt2. Test framework credit and parent-selection changes separately; richer mechanism descriptions or diagnostics would require a general interface and a fresh matched study.
causal_test_not_launched: A future public-development component ablation could change only repair/reject handling or proposal distribution, with fixed selected source and repeated score readings. Do not treat such a program ablation as proof of framework superiority.
